label: EMPA-REG OUTCOME (NEJM 2015)
title: Empagliflozin, Cardiovascular Outcomes, and Mortality in Type 2 Diabetes
abstract: The effects of empagliflozin, an inhibitor of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2, in addition to standard care, on cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in patients with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk are not known. We randomly assigned patients to receive 10 mg or 25 mg of empagliflozin or placebo once daily. The primary composite outcome was death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke, as analyzed in the pooled empagliflozin group versus the placebo group. The key secondary composite outcome was the primary outcome plus hospitalization for unstable angina. A total of 7020 patients were treated, with a median observation time of 3.1 years. The primary outcome occurred in a significantly lower proportion of patients in the empagliflozin group than in the placebo group, with a hazard ratio in the empagliflozin group of 0.86 (95.02% confidence interval, 0.74 to 0.99; P=0.04 for superiority). There were no significant between-group differences in the rates of myocardial infarction or stroke, but in the empagliflozin group there were significantly lower rates of death from cardiovascular causes (3.7%, vs. 5.9% in the placebo group; 38% relative risk reduction), hospitalization for heart failure (2.7% and 4.1%, respectively; 35% relative risk reduction), and death from any cause (5.7% and 8.3%, respectively; 32% relative risk reduction). There was no significant between-group difference in the key secondary outcome. Among patients with type 2 diabetes at high risk for cardiovascular events who received empagliflozin, as compared with placebo, there was a lower rate of the primary composite cardiovascular outcome and of death from any cause when the study drug was added to standard care.
notes: Landmark cardiovascular outcomes trial; NEJM 2015 JIF ~70–96 across years.

label: Global DALYs (Lancet GBD-style)
title: Global, regional, and national disability-adjusted life-years for 354 diseases and injuries
abstract: Background: The Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study provides a comprehensive assessment of health loss from a standardised set of causes. Quantifying the burden in terms of disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) allows for comparisons across populations, diseases, and time. Methods: We estimated DALYs for 354 causes of death and disability across 195 countries and territories using vital registration data, verbal autopsies, surveillance systems, and household surveys. Years of life lost were calculated using cause-specific mortality estimates and a reference life table. Years lived with disability were estimated by multiplying prevalence by disability weights for each sequela. We used a Bayesian meta-regression tool to synthesise heterogeneous data sources. Findings: Total DALYs declined globally from 2.8 billion in 1990 to 2.5 billion in the most recent year, despite population growth and ageing. Non-communicable diseases accounted for an increasing share of total DALYs, while communicable, maternal, neonatal, and nutritional causes continued to decline in most regions. Cardiovascular diseases, neoplasms, and mental disorders were leading contributors to non-communicable disease burden. Geographic disparities widened for several conditions, with sub-Saharan Africa experiencing disproportionately high DALYs from infectious and maternal causes. Interpretation: Sustained progress against communicable disease has not been matched by equivalent gains against non-communicable disease, and large inequities persist between high-income and low-income settings. Health systems and financing strategies must adapt to the changing burden profile to meet Sustainable Development Goal targets.
notes: Plausible Lancet-tier global burden of disease descriptive epidemiology.

label: Breast cancer screening RCT (JAMA-style)
title: Outcomes of Risk-Stratified vs Annual Mammography Screening in Average-Risk Women
abstract: Importance: Annual mammography screening has been the standard recommendation for women at average risk of breast cancer, yet evidence on the benefit-harm tradeoff of risk-stratified screening intervals remains limited. Objective: To compare cancer detection, false-positive recall, and interval cancer rates between a risk-stratified screening strategy and annual mammography in women aged 50 to 74 years at average risk of breast cancer. Design, Setting, and Participants: Pragmatic cluster-randomised trial conducted at 38 community imaging centres across four regions, enrolling 42,180 women between 2018 and 2022 with follow-up through 2025. Interventions: Participants were randomised by site to either annual digital mammography or a risk-stratified protocol assigning 1-, 2-, or 3-year intervals based on a validated polygenic and clinical risk score. Main Outcomes and Measures: Cumulative invasive cancer detection rate, recall rate per screening episode, interval cancer rate within 24 months of a negative screen, and stage distribution at diagnosis. Results: Over a median follow-up of 4.6 years, invasive cancer detection was non-inferior in the risk-stratified group compared with annual screening, with comparable stage distributions. Recall rates were significantly lower under risk stratification, while interval cancer rates were similar between groups. Conclusions and Relevance: Risk-stratified mammography intervals achieved equivalent cancer detection with fewer false-positive recalls, supporting a personalised screening approach in average-risk women.
notes: Plausible JAMA-tier pragmatic RCT; JAMA JIF ~50–63.

label: Surgical site infection bundle (Annals-style)
title: A Multimodal Bundle to Reduce Surgical Site Infections After Colorectal Surgery
abstract: Background: Surgical site infections after elective colorectal surgery remain a leading source of postoperative morbidity, prolonged length of stay, and readmission. Prior single-component interventions have shown inconsistent effectiveness. Objective: To evaluate whether a multimodal infection-prevention bundle reduces 30-day surgical site infection rates compared with usual perioperative care. Design: Stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial. Setting: 14 academic and community hospitals across three health systems. Participants: 6,842 adults undergoing elective colorectal resection between 2021 and 2024. Intervention: A bundle comprising oral and intravenous antibiotic prophylaxis, chlorhexidine bathing, intraoperative wound protectors, glycemic control, and standardised dressing protocols, supported by audit and feedback. Measurements: The primary outcome was 30-day surgical site infection ascertained through standardised chart review. Secondary outcomes included readmission, length of stay, and antimicrobial resistance among isolates. Results: Crude surgical site infection rates declined from 11.4% in the baseline period to 6.8% after full bundle implementation. After adjustment for secular trends and case mix, the bundle was associated with a relative reduction of approximately 35%. Readmissions and length of stay also declined modestly, with no detectable increase in resistance among recovered isolates. Limitations: Open-label design and heterogeneity in baseline compliance. Conclusions: Implementation of a standardised multimodal bundle was associated with clinically meaningful reductions in surgical site infections, supporting broader adoption in colorectal surgery programs.
notes: Plausible Annals of Internal Medicine tier (JIF ~20–40).

label: Adjuvant immunotherapy in stage III melanoma (Lancet Oncol-style)
title: Adjuvant Anti-PD-1 Plus Targeted Therapy in Resected Stage III Melanoma: A Randomised Phase 3 Trial
abstract: Background: Adjuvant anti-PD-1 monotherapy improves recurrence-free survival in patients with resected stage III melanoma, but distant metastasis rates remain substantial. Combining anti-PD-1 with BRAF/MEK inhibition may further reduce recurrence in patients with BRAF V600 mutations. Methods: In this international, multicentre, randomised, open-label phase 3 trial, we enrolled adults with completely resected BRAF V600-mutant stage IIIB-D melanoma. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to receive adjuvant anti-PD-1 monotherapy for 12 months or anti-PD-1 plus dabrafenib and trametinib for 12 months. The primary endpoint was recurrence-free survival; secondary endpoints included distant metastasis-free survival, overall survival, and safety. Findings: Between 2020 and 2024, 1,108 patients were randomised. After a median follow-up of 34 months, the combination arm demonstrated significantly improved recurrence-free survival compared with monotherapy, with a hazard ratio of 0.68 (95% CI 0.55–0.84). Distant metastasis-free survival also favoured the combination. Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were more common with the combination, predominantly pyrexia, transaminitis, and immune-mediated events. Quality-of-life scores were comparable between groups by month 6. Interpretation: Adjuvant combination of anti-PD-1 with BRAF/MEK inhibition improved recurrence-free survival in resected BRAF V600-mutant stage III melanoma at the cost of increased toxicity, supporting consideration as a new adjuvant standard for selected patients with adequate organ function and access to multidisciplinary toxicity management.

label: Heart failure registry analysis (Circulation-style)
title: Real-World Initiation of SGLT2 Inhibitors in Patients Hospitalised for Heart Failure
abstract: Background: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors reduce cardiovascular mortality and heart failure hospitalisations across the ejection fraction spectrum, yet real-world initiation during index hospitalisations has lagged behind guideline recommendations. Methods: Using a multicentre electronic health record registry of adults hospitalised with a primary diagnosis of heart failure between 2021 and 2024, we examined temporal trends in in-hospital initiation of SGLT2 inhibitors, predictors of initiation, and 90-day clinical outcomes. Patients were stratified by ejection fraction phenotype and baseline kidney function. Multivariable logistic regression identified patient, clinician, and hospital factors associated with initiation. Inverse probability weighting was used to estimate associations between in-hospital initiation and a composite of 90-day all-cause readmission and death. Results: Among 28,940 eligible hospitalisations, in-hospital SGLT2 inhibitor initiation rose from 9% in early 2021 to 41% by late 2024. Initiation was lower in patients with chronic kidney disease, older age, and at non-teaching hospitals. After adjustment, in-hospital initiation was associated with a 17% relative reduction in the composite 90-day outcome, with consistent effects across ejection fraction strata. Conclusions: Uptake of SGLT2 inhibitor initiation during heart failure hospitalisations has accelerated but remains incomplete, particularly in vulnerable subgroups including older adults, those with chronic kidney disease, and patients managed at non-teaching hospitals. Closing implementation gaps could yield meaningful short-term clinical benefit.

label: ED triage ML retrospective (mid-tier specialty)
title: Development of a Machine Learning Triage Score for Emergency Department Admission Prediction
abstract: Background: Accurate early prediction of hospital admission at emergency department triage may improve patient flow, resource allocation, and crowding. Existing triage tools rely on coarse acuity categories that incompletely capture admission risk. Objective: To develop and internally validate a machine learning model that estimates the probability of inpatient admission at the moment of triage using only information routinely available within five minutes of registration. Methods: We performed a retrospective cohort study of 184,260 adult emergency department visits across three hospitals from 2019 to 2024. Candidate predictors included demographics, vital signs, chief complaint, mode of arrival, and brief medical history flags. Gradient boosting and logistic regression models were trained using temporal split validation and compared on discrimination, calibration, and decision-curve net benefit. Subgroup analyses examined performance across age, sex, and presenting complaint clusters. Results: The gradient boosting model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.84 with good calibration. Decision-curve analysis demonstrated greater net benefit than triage acuity alone across a wide range of decision thresholds. Performance was stable across subgroups, with slightly lower discrimination in patients with non-specific complaints. Conclusions: A machine learning triage score using only data available at registration achieved good discrimination and calibration for emergency department admission prediction. Prospective implementation studies are needed to evaluate operational impact.
notes: Plausible mid-tier emergency medicine / informatics journal (JIF ~3–8).

label: Clinical microbiology workflow (J Clin Microbiol-style)
title: Evaluation of a Rapid Multiplex PCR Workflow for Bloodstream Infection Identification
abstract: Background: Timely identification of bloodstream pathogens is essential for appropriate antimicrobial selection and improved outcomes in patients with sepsis. Conventional culture-based workflows often require 24 to 72 hours for organism identification and antimicrobial susceptibility profiling. Objective: To evaluate the analytical performance and turnaround time of a rapid multiplex PCR workflow for bloodstream infection identification compared with standard culture-based methods. Methods: This was a prospective, multicentre, head-to-head comparison conducted at four tertiary hospital microbiology laboratories. Positive blood culture bottles were tested in parallel using the multiplex PCR assay and reference culture-based identification with antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Discordant results were adjudicated using 16S rRNA sequencing. Primary outcomes included sensitivity, specificity, and time to organism identification. Secondary outcomes included detection of resistance markers and estimated impact on time to effective therapy. Results: A total of 1,486 positive blood culture bottles were analysed. Sensitivity for on-panel organisms exceeded 96%, with specificity above 99% for the most common targets. Median time to identification was reduced from 38 hours to 1.5 hours. Detection of methicillin and carbapenem resistance markers showed high concordance with phenotypic testing. Conclusions: Adoption of this rapid multiplex PCR workflow substantially reduced time to organism identification while maintaining accuracy comparable with conventional methods.
notes: Plausible Journal of Clinical Microbiology-tier workflow paper (JIF ~5–9).

label: Retrospective cohort, general low-mid tier (PLoS ONE-style)
title: Association Between Sleep Duration and Glycemic Control in Adults with Type 2 Diabetes
abstract: Background: Sleep duration has been implicated as a modifiable risk factor for glycemic dysregulation in patients with type 2 diabetes, but findings have been inconsistent across populations and assessment methods. Objective: To examine the association between self-reported sleep duration and hemoglobin A1c in a community-based cohort of adults with type 2 diabetes. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis using linked primary care electronic health records and a regional health survey administered between 2020 and 2023. Adults aged 30 to 75 years with prevalent type 2 diabetes and at least one A1c measurement within 90 days of survey completion were included. Sleep duration was self-reported as habitual hours per night and categorised as short, normal, or long. Multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, diabetes duration, glucose-lowering medications, and depressive symptoms. Subgroup analyses examined effect modification by insulin use. Results: Among 4,820 participants, short sleep duration was associated with modestly higher A1c levels compared with normal sleep duration, while long sleep duration showed a smaller, less consistent association. Effect estimates were attenuated after adjustment for depressive symptoms and body mass index but remained statistically significant for short sleep. Conclusions: Short habitual sleep duration was independently associated with worse glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes, supporting attention to sleep hygiene within diabetes care.
notes: Plausible PLoS ONE / BMC-tier observational cohort (JIF ~2–4).

label: Preprint, mechanistic biology (bioRxiv-style)
title: A Conserved Lipid Sensor Module Regulates Hepatic Lipid Droplet Maturation
abstract: Background: Hepatic lipid droplets serve as central organelles for lipid storage and mobilisation, yet the molecular determinants of droplet maturation under metabolic stress remain incompletely understood. Recent work has implicated several membrane-embedded sensor proteins, but their functional hierarchy is unclear. Methods: We combined CRISPR interference screens, proximity labelling proteomics, and in vivo high-fat diet models to identify regulators of lipid droplet maturation in primary hepatocytes and intact liver. Candidate hits were validated using engineered cell lines, fluorescence microscopy, and lipidomics. Mechanistic studies employed reconstituted membrane systems and structural modelling. Results: We identified a conserved three-protein module that acts as a graded lipid sensor controlling droplet expansion, monolayer composition, and recruitment of lipases. Loss of the module impaired droplet maturation, sensitised hepatocytes to lipotoxic stress, and exacerbated steatosis in mice fed a high-fat diet. Reconstitution experiments demonstrated direct binding to specific phospholipid species, and structural modelling suggested a conformational switch coupling lipid binding to downstream effector recruitment. Pharmacological mimicry of the active conformation reduced steatosis severity in a pilot in vivo experiment. Conclusions: A conserved lipid sensor module regulates hepatic lipid droplet maturation and represents a candidate therapeutic node for steatotic liver disease. This manuscript has not yet undergone peer review.
notes: Preprint without a confirmed venue; landing journal range is wide (specialty journal to high-tier mechanistic).
